title: Latent bug hypotheses and next steps (post-merge)
content:
Quick context:
- This is a personal scratchpad collecting what I saw after merging PR #3045 (session-kv-cache-optim). Not a final writeup — rough, partial, intended for triage and experiments.

Observed signal (what triggered this):
- Over the 48h post-merge window (canary -> prod), we saw a small but consistent uptick in tail latency for chat requests with long context (>2048 tokens). 95th/99th increased by ~15-25% vs baseline.
- Error rate (5xx) for the same traffic slice remained low, but a few customer reports mentioned unexpected token repetition in generated outputs.
- CPU usage on serving nodes stayed nominal; GPU time per token slightly increased for affected requests.
- Correlated with higher cache eviction counts in the KV cache metrics (evictions spiked right after deploy).

Immediate hypotheses (ranked, quick notes):
1) Cache eviction thrash due to different token-keying semantics introduced in PR3045
   - PR changed the key derivation to include a short timestamp/nonce for concurrency safety in streaming. Possibly increased key entropy -> lower hit rate -> more recomputation.
   - Explains increased GPU time per token (misses), higher evictions. Also could cause repetition if the model is recomputing prefixes under different internal states.
2) Inadvertent change to LRU weighting policy when sequence splits occur
   - New logic for "partial-kv flush on incremental segment" may mark items as cold incorrectly. Look at cache.prometheus label kv_lru_score.*
   - Would cause older keys to be removed sooner, hitting long-context sessions.
3) Edge-case in streaming join logic causes double-requesting of last chunk (duplicate prefix sent)
   - Could look like repetition in output if the runtime requests overlapping prefixes. Would not necessarily bump 5xx but increases latency and GPU work.

Quick repro plan (local-ish):
- Build a small harness that mimics long-chat session traffic: sequence lengths 2500-6000 tokens, with periodic streaming flushes. Use same batching profile as prod.
- Two variants: with PR3045 changes vs revert (local branch revert commit). Run both on same hardware (dev-gpu-small) and capture: KV hit rate, eviction counts, per-token GPU time, and raw logs.
- Controlled load generator: 10 concurrent sessions, 50 req/s, run for 30 minutes to get steady-state.

Instrumentation to add (short-term):
- Add debug-level metric: kv_key_entropy (histogram of key lengths / distinct keys per session-id).
- Track per-session cache hit/miss ratio (label: session_id truncated).
- Log a SHA/short-hash of the computed KV key when a miss occurs (sanitized) to see if non-determinism introduced.
- Add a flag to metric: streaming_overlap_detected when codepath observes two overlapping prefix requests.

Minimal experiments (ordered):
A) Toggle the nonce/timestamp inclusion off (config flag) in a canary subset (5% traffic). Measure hit rate and tail latency. If improved, high confidence hypothesis #1.
B) Revert only the LRU-score tweak in a canary to test hypothesis #2.
C) Add temporary dedupe in streaming join: drop identical prefix requests within 10ms window. If repetition and GPU work drop, points to #3.

Possible quick fixes (low-risk):
- Feature flag to disable nonce/timestamp key change (should be quick revert).
- Increase cache max-size temporarily for long-context sessions by 20% while we evaluate. (Ops + cost tradeoff).
- Add additional logging (no behavioral change) and run for 24-72h to collect evidence.

Longer-term work items (for planning):
- Rework key derivation to be stable per-session+offset while still supporting concurrency (design doc needed). Owner: Asha.
- Add better session-level cache metrics and tracing to correlate model outputs -> specific KV keys. Owner: Priya.
- Run batch of synthetic long-context benchmarks across model catalog to quantify base hit-rate expectations and tune defaults. Owner: Felix.

Suggested PRs/branches to open (titles + short description + rough ETA):
- pr/eval/disable-nonce-kvkey - experiment: toggle to revert nonce inclusion (Felix) - ETA: 1 day to get canary running
- pr/telemetry/session-kv-metrics - add per-session hit/miss counters and key-hash logging (Priya) - ETA: 3 days
- pr/fix/lru-score-boundary - revert LRU score change and add unit tests around segment splits (Asha) - ETA: 3-5 days

Acceptance criteria for fixes / triage closure:
- Restore 95th/99th latency for long-context cohort to within 5% of pre-PR baseline for 48h on canary (5-10% traffic)
- No increase in token-repeat complaints from customers in the same window
- Observable increase in cache hit rate (or stable with compensation like increased capacity)

Notes / open questions (stuff to ask on triage):
- Did PR3045 include any rolling-config changes to cache size defaults? (I think not, but verify).
- Are there other recent PRs touching streaming join behavior that merged near the same time? Check PR timeline between 3041-3055.
- Is the observed repetition reproducible with the logged seed used by the generator? I need a deterministic run to rule out model sampling variance.

Meeting / next steps (my suggestion):
- Quick async triage thread: post signal + this doc to #eng-serving-runtime today, tag Asha + Priya.
- If we can flip a config flag quickly, run canary A (disable nonce) and observe for 6-12h. If improvement, promote to 20% and continue.
- If no improvement, run LRU revert next.

Todo (me):
- [ ] finalize canary config and open pr/eval/disable-nonce-kvkey (1 day)
- [ ] write simple harness for long-context perf runs (Felix) (0.5 day)
- [ ] add minimal per-session metric patch (Priya) (coordinate)
- [ ] gather exact customer example(s) for token repetition (CS)

Random scribbles (keep here):
- If key entropy is high because of nonce, then alternative is to attach nonce to concurrency token only (not to base prefix key) -> need small refactor so that multiple concurrent streams share baseline cache while still marking in-flight updates.
- For experiments, ensure we test both with and without batching — batching interacts badly with keying if keys include timestamps.

End scratchpad. Will iterate and convert to a formal postmortem if we get clear evidence pointing to a single root cause.
